newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower as funds ditch base metals.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower as funds ditch base metals.

text.p: COMEX copper settled sharply lower Monday as funds bailed out of the base metals markets, pushing the May contract to its weakest close in seven weeks.

Brokers said speculative selling on the first day of aluminum futures trading on Tokyo's Commodity Exchange prompted funds to begin selling early on LME and the bearish sentiment spilled over into COMEX.
"There was some consumer hedge buying which softened the blow," said Fred Demler of E. D. & F. Man International.
The technical picture indicated that the market was oversold, but prices may not have reached their lows yet, Demler added.
May COMEX settled down 3.55 cents at 104.75 cents a lb, traded 106.30 to 104.40 cents. Spot April went out 3.40 cents lower at 106.50 cents.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots compared to Friday's 9,367 lots.
The cash to three months backwardation on LME shrank some $10 to $30/$35.
Some traders suggested that funds needed to sell their base metals positions to raise cash to compensate for losses incurred during the slide on Wall Street.
On Monday, the LME began reporting stocks on a daily basis. Copper inventory fell 875 tonnes to 173,600 tonnes.
COMEX copper stocks on Monday fell 237 short tons to 42,072 short tons.
Brokers said that despite the rout in futures prices, demand on the physical market remained firm in the U.S. especially.

The physical market was being underpinned by quality problems at some Chilean SX/EW plants due to the drought, and further support would came later this month when Kennecott shut its Utah smelter for maintenance, brokers said.
